paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The figure illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Structured Dense Pseudo Attention) output values concerning different layers, specifically with a threshold of \(1 \times 10^{-3}\). 

On the X-axis, labeled "Layer," a linear scale is used, ranging from 0 to 22, with integer intervals indicating the number of layers. The Y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio," also with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 1, displaying the proportion of output values that fall below the specified threshold.

There are three distinct lines on the graph, each representing different sparsity ratios:

1. A blue dashed line depicts the sparsity ratio before gating, which generally starts at approximately 0.9 at layer 0 and steadily decreases, reaching a nearly flat position at around 0.003.
   
2. An orange dotted line represents the sparsity ratio after the gate. It shows a higher average sparsity of about 0.126 and decreases from layer 0 to around layer 12, where it stabilizes at a lower value.

3. A green dashed line illustrates the sparsity ratio after the average gate, exhibiting an average of 0.080. This line also starts higher and descends, demonstrating a similar trend to the other two but with less steepness before leveling off.

Specific observations include that starting around layer 3, all lines decline, with noticeable changes occurring between layers 0 and 5 for each ratio. The graph provides visual insights into the impact of gating on sparsity ratios across layers.
model_annotations.Chinese:
The graph illustrates the sparsity ratios of the output from a Stochastic Deep Projection Attention (SDPA) across different layers, specifically focusing on the effect of a threshold of \(1 \times 10^{-3}\). The x-axis, labeled "Layer," represents layer numbers ranging from 0 to 22, while the y-axis, labeled "Sparsity Ratio," quantifies the fraction of output values that fall below the specified threshold, with values ranging from 0 to 0.9.

Three lines represent different conditions: the dashed blue line denotes the sparsity ratio before gating, which starts at approximately 0.8 for Layer 0 and decreases sharply to close to 0 by Layer 10. The dotted orange line represents the sparsity ratio after gating, beginning at about 0.75 and gradually declining to around 0.1 at Layer 22. Finally, the dashed green line indicates the sparsity ratio after applying an average gate, which starts slightly below the orange line and stabilizes around 0.08, reflecting minimal change after Layer 10, with slight fluctuations thereafter. Each line provides key insights into how sparsity ratios evolve through the layers under different conditions.
model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of the output from Sparse Dynamic Programming Attention (SDPA) across different layers, specifically at a threshold of 1e-3. The x-axis is labeled "Layer" and employs a linear scale ranging from 0 to 22, with tick marks at regular integer intervals. The y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 1, with tick marks at regular intervals. Three lines are represented in the plot: the dashed blue line, which corresponds to the sparsity ratio before gating, remains above 0.8 from layer 0 to around layer 2, then exhibits a steady decline to near 0 by layer 22; the dotted orange line, representing the sparsity ratio after gating, starts at approximately 0.8 at layer 0 and decreases to about 0.1 by layer 22 with various fluctuations in between; and the dashed green line, indicating the sparsity ratio after the average gate, begins at approximately 0.4 and gradually declines, leveling off close to 0.08 after layer 10. Each line distinctly illustrates changes in sparsity across the layers, providing insights into the effect of gating on the SDPA output.
model_annotations.German:
Das Diagramm zeigt das Verhältnis der Sparsität der SDPA-Ausgaben in Abhängigkeit von der Schicht (Layer). Auf der x-Achse ist die Schicht nummeriert, ohne spezifische Einheiten oder Einschränkungen, räumlich zwischen 0 und 22, wobei die genauen Tick-Beschriftungen nicht angegeben sind. Die y-Achse stellt die Sparsitätsrate dar, die von 0 bis 1 reicht, wobei die Tick-Beschriftungen ebenfalls nicht numerisch angeordnet sind.

Drei Linien sind im Diagramm dargestellt. Die gestrichelte, hellblaue Linie zeigt die Sparsitätsrate vor dem Gate, die an der y-Achse bei etwa 0,8 beginnt und dann stark auf etwa 0,0 abfällt, mit einem stabilen Trend, das Ende bei Layer 22 zu erreichen. Die orangefarbene, gepunktete Linie symbolisiert die Sparsitätsrate nach dem Gate, die bei etwa 0,9 beginnt und auf etwa 0,1 abfällt. Diese Linie zeigt einen leichten Rückgang mit einer stabilen Tendenz. Schließlich zeigt die grüne, gestrichelte Linie die Sparsitätsrate nach der Durchschnittsbildung des Gates, die ähnlich zu der orangefarbenen Linie verläuft, jedoch insgesamt bei etwa 0,08 endet.
